blockers.title: The per-row name swap sets both name confidences to 100, which silently clears low-confidence flags
blockers.scenario: Proven by probe A. Take a surname-first row with an undecided order, read as 'Esposito'(92) 'Giulia'(50). Before the swap the review shows 1 row to review and 1 'Da controllare'. After a tap on 'Scambia nome e cognome riga 1' it shows 0 rows to review, 0 flags and 1 ready. The given name read at 50 is saved as if checked, although its field was never focused or edited. The swap also sets nameReading.acknowledged=true. That clears the compound-split confirmation too: a provisional 'De' / 'Luca Mario' split becomes surname 'De', given name 'Luca Mario', and the row is ready.
blockers.specReference: 01_PRODUCT_SPEC.md §3.6 (confidence is field-level; low-confidence text stays marked; flagged fields clear only when edited or acknowledged by focus-leave); 04_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md (keep every low-confidence reading visible and marked)
blockers.suggestedFix: Swap the confidence values and acknowledgedFields together with the text instead of setting them to 100. Keep compoundAmbiguity pending unless the row has exactly two words.

blockers.title: A manual age correction within one year of a stored birth date is silently discarded, and minor status is saved the opposite way
blockers.scenario: Proven by probe B and its reverse. The birth date 2008-08-01 is read confidently. With course start 2026-08-29 the review shows age 18. The operator types 17. ageConflictsWithStoredDate allows ±1, so the row has no flag and stays ready, and the date field stays hidden. commitCandidates saves the date with declaredAgeAtCourseStart=null, so the stored student is an adult (isStudentMinor=false) although the review showed 17. The other direction also fails: a date giving 17 with a typed 18 is saved as a minor. The operator cannot see that a date overrides the entry.
blockers.specReference: 01_PRODUCT_SPEC.md §3.1 and §3.6 (an entered age means completed years on the first course day; minor status on that day); AGENTS.md §11/§3 (no inconsistent state between review and storage)
blockers.suggestedFix: When ageManuallyEdited is set, treat any difference from the date-derived age as a conflict. Show the date and require the operator to correct or clear it, or explicitly accept replacing it with the declared age. Keep the ±1 slack only for a printed age.

blockers.title: A printed age below 70 'corroborates' a date below 70; neither blocks the row and the age reading is never marked
blockers.scenario: Proven by the corroboration probe. The date 2008-03-10 is read at confidence 40 and the printed age 17 at confidence 30. The counters show 0 rows to review and 1 ready. The age field has aria-invalid=false and no 'Da controllare'; the date shows only 'Lettura incerta' and is not counted. The save stores the date, so the student is an adult (isStudentMinor=false) while the review showed 17. studentScanAgeCorroborated never checks ageReading.confidence, so two sub-threshold readings clear each other. This goes beyond the accepted S5 limitation, which assumes the independent age reading is reliable.
blockers.specReference: 04_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md (every low-confidence reading stays visible and marked); 01_PRODUCT_SPEC.md §3.6 (a reliable date corroborates the printed age); .evidence/S5/domain-review.json (accepted limitation scope)
blockers.suggestedFix: Require ageReading.confidence >= MIN_FIELD_CONFIDENCE to corroborate. Mark a sub-threshold age reading in ageNeedsReview even when a date exists. Show the age that will actually be stored, or flag it when it differs from the displayed age.

blockers.title: Two-letter surname particles (Lo, Li; also El, Al) are silently deleted and the row is saved with a confident wrong surname
blockers.scenario: Proven by parser probe 1 with real TSV geometry. 'Lo Bardino Marco' on a surname-first sheet becomes surname 'Bardino', given name 'Marco'. Confidence is 95/95, compoundAmbiguity=false, sex is inferred and the date and age are kept, so the row is ready. nameReading.raw is 'Bardino Marco', so 'Lo' is not visible anywhere. 'Li Carrasi Anna' and given-first 'Marco Lo Bardino' fail the same way. isNameToken drops every token under three letters that is not in SURNAME_PARTICLES, and that set has 'la' but not 'lo' or 'li'. A two-letter surname or given name on its own (for example Re, Wu, Li) is also discarded; the field comes out empty and flagged, so the read text is lost.
blockers.specReference: 01_PRODUCT_SPEC.md §3.6 (preserve the recognized name; never make a shown reading blank); 04_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md S4 (particle rules; ambiguous cases visible); reviewer brief: no reading may be silently dropped
blockers.suggestedFix: Add lo, li, el, al (and review the rest of the set) to SURNAME_PARTICLES. More generally, keep every short alphabetic token that sits between name words in raw and words, and mark the row compoundAmbiguity instead of deleting the token.

importantFindings.title: The sex suggestion goes stale and is not gated by confidence: swapping or editing a name keeps the old guess
importantFindings.scenario: Proven by probe A: the sex inferred from the surname 'Esposito' (male) survives the per-row swap, and 'Giulia Esposito' is saved as male with no sex flag. applyStudentNameOrder infers sex from a given name below 70, although candidateFromLine deliberately gates that. Probe 1 shows 'Lcua' at confidence 0 getting 'female'. updateField never recomputes the suggestion after the operator fixes the name.
importantFindings.specReference: 01_PRODUCT_SPEC.md §3.6 (sex inference is only a convenience); studentScan.ts:836-838 comment (a guess from an unreliable name is worse than none)
importantFindings.suggestedFix: Record whether sex was inferred. On a swap or a name edit, re-infer it or clear it if it was never touched by the operator. Gate the inference in applyStudentNameOrder by MIN_FIELD_CONFIDENCE.

importantFindings.title: The date-of-birth field disappears after its first valid change and cannot be reopened once cleared
importantFindings.scenario: Proven in jsdom by probe C. A flagged date (confidence 50) is visible. The first valid change sets confidence to 100 and the field unmounts. On desktop Chrome, typing '1' of '15' into the day segment already produces 2014-02-01, so the second keystroke is lost and the day 01 is saved invisibly. The iOS picker fires input events the same way. Clearing the field (the picker's Clear, or Backspace) removes the only date input. The row is then saved age-only ({dateOfBirth:'', declaredAgeAtCourseStart:12}) and the read date cannot be re-entered in the review.
importantFindings.specReference: 01_PRODUCT_SPEC.md §3.6 (rows and fields are editable; recognized text stays visible); AGENTS.md §9
importantFindings.suggestedFix: Keep the date field mounted for the rest of the review once it has been shown or edited, for example with a 'dateTouched' flag. Offer a way to restore the original reading.

importantFindings.title: Tapping the 'righe da controllare' counter repeatedly acknowledges every flagged field without any edit
importantFindings.scenario: Proven by probe D. Three rows each have a surname read at confidence 40, and the counters start at [3,0,0]. Four taps on 'Vai alla prima riga da controllare' change them to [0,0,3], and 'Aggiungi 3 allievi' saves. Each tap focuses the next flagged field programmatically; the next tap blurs it, and the blur counts as acknowledgement.
importantFindings.specReference: 01_PRODUCT_SPEC.md §3.6 (acknowledgement means leaving a field the operator focused; counters only navigate)
importantFindings.suggestedFix: Do not let focus given by counter navigation arm acknowledgement. Require a user-initiated focus (pointer or keyboard in the field) or an edit.

importantFindings.title: A year of five or more digits in the date field crashes the render and loses the whole review
importantFindings.scenario: Proven by probe E. The HTML date input accepts years with 4+ digits; desktop Chrome allows up to 6. Typing '20140-02-16' makes ageConflictsWithStoredDate call calculateAge, and parseDateOnly throws 'Invalid date-only value'. The app has no error boundary, so the tree unmounts and every reviewed row is lost. The invariant checker does not validate the date format either.
importantFindings.specReference: AGENTS.md §11 (invalid values detected, not crashing); 01_PRODUCT_SPEC.md §10 (routine errors stay in context)
importantFindings.suggestedFix: Check the date with /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/ in updateField and treat anything else as an invalid, flagged draft. Guard calculateAge callers in the review, and add a date-format check to invariants.ts.

importantFindings.title: A remembered course name order silently overrides the new sheet's own vote
importantFindings.scenario: Proven by probe F. The course has 'surname-given' remembered. A given-first sheet of 4 rows is scanned. No order question appears, the counters show [0,0,4], and all four are saved swapped with confident values. The sheet's own inference is computed and then thrown away.
importantFindings.specReference: 01_PRODUCT_SPEC.md §3.6 (infer one order per sheet; explicit whole-sheet correction)
importantFindings.suggestedFix: When the sheet's own vote is decisive and disagrees with the remembered order, ask. Or treat the remembered order only as a tie-breaker.

importantFindings.title: An unsaved scan review is thrown away without confirmation by another image, a retake or Back
importantFindings.scenario: Proven by probe G. The operator corrects page-1 rows, then uses 'Scegli un’altra immagine' for page 2. Page 1 is replaced with no dialog. An in-app back tap or a phone Back or edge swipe unmounts StudentScan the same way. Up to 40 reviewed rows are lost.
importantFindings.specReference: 01_PRODUCT_SPEC.md §10 (routine errors stay in context); 04_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md F1 (analogous explicit discard before navigation)
importantFindings.suggestedFix: Confirm before discarding a review that has candidates. Consider appending a second image's rows instead of replacing them.

importantFindings.title: One line with a personnel keyword silently drops every following row
importantFindings.scenario: Proven by parser probe 1. A header 'Segreteria didattica: 0212345678' above the table gives 0 of 4 students, and the sheet is reported as 'Immagine poco leggibile'; every retake fails the same way. A 'volontario' word in a name cell before the phone keeps 1 of 5 students, and the other 4 disappear without any cue. The mode lasts until an 'allievi', 'studenti' or 'partecipanti' heading.
importantFindings.specReference: 01_PRODUCT_SPEC.md §3.6 (variable-layout sheet; no silent omission); reviewer brief (no reading silently dropped)
importantFindings.suggestedFix: Enter personnel mode only on a line that is purely a heading (no name cell and no structured fields), or only below the table band. Report the count of rows skipped as personnel or heading.

importantFindings.title: The heading-keyword drop also removes students whose given name is a keyword (e.g. Domenica)
importantFindings.scenario: Proven by parser probe 1: 'Bardino Domenica' with a date and age disappears, giving 3 of 4 candidates, with no trace. This extends the S4 limitation recorded for surnames. It also covers real surnames in the list such as Sabato, Corso and Stampa.
importantFindings.specReference: 04_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md S4 known limitations; reviewer brief (no silent drop)
importantFindings.suggestedFix: Do not apply the keyword test to a line that has name-cell geometry plus a date, age or phone. Otherwise keep the row as a flagged review row.

importantFindings.title: The staff role code is ignored when fewer than three rows carry structured words, or when the role column is on the right
importantFindings.scenario: Proven by parser probe 1. A tight crop has one student row and one staff row 'Bardino Luca IS 3331234567 34 anni 03/04/1992'. inferPageLayout returns null, isPersonnelRow returns false, and the staff member comes out with confidence 95, sex, date and age: a ready student. A layout with the role column right of the date is also never detected. This extends the S4 one-line staff limitation: here the role code is actually read.
importantFindings.specReference: Reviewer brief (staff rows must not be ready students without review); 04_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md S4 known limitations
importantFindings.suggestedFix: Without a layout, still flag any row with an all-caps role token after the first word. With a layout, look for role codes anywhere in the row.

importantFindings.title: When two rows are read as one line, only the first date, age and phone are kept, and the only warning is a 'compound name'
importantFindings.scenario: Mechanism proven by probe 5; the trigger (Tesseract joining two table rows, for example under skew) is speculative. The candidate becomes 'Fornace Sara Paolo' / 'Pellandi'. The second student's date, age and phone are silently discarded. The only prompt is 'Nome o cognome composto', and confirming it merges two real students into one.
importantFindings.specReference: Reviewer brief (two real students never become one; no reading dropped)
importantFindings.suggestedFix: When a line has two or more dates, ages or phones, or four or more name words with duplicate structured fields, flag it as possibly merged rows. Show all the readings and offer a split.

importantFindings.title: Fragment joining checks only local uniqueness, so a systematic drift shifts every date to the next student
importantFindings.scenario: Mechanism proven by probe 4; the trigger is speculative. Row pitch is 80 px with 24 px words, the age and date are in a separate block, and they drift 66 px (about 5° over 750 px). Four of five students receive their neighbour's date and age at confidence 95. Row 1 loses its date and an orphan date row appears at the end.
importantFindings.specReference: 04_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md S4 (join only when row geometry supports it)
importantFindings.suggestedFix: Reject a join when its offset exceeds about 0.25 × medianPitch, or when the median offset across all fragments is far from zero.

qolFindings.title: A zero-confidence name word takes another word's confidence
qolFindings.scenario: Proven by probe 1: 'Bardino' plus 'Lcua' at confidence 0 comes out with firstName confidence 95, through the `|| candidate.confidence.firstName` fallback. averageNameConfidence also ignores zeros, so they never lower a field. Whether Tesseract actually emits a confidence of exactly 0 for a word is speculative.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: Treat 0 as a real reading whenever word geometry exists (exactConfidence), and do not fall back to another word's confidence.

qolFindings.title: The eraser runs synchronously on the main thread; grainy images take several seconds
qolFindings.scenario: Proven by probe 3 on a 2600×1900 synthetic grainy image: 0.7 s at σ=6, 2.4 s at σ=15 and 6.8 s at σ=25 in desktop Node, so roughly four times that on a phone. The progress bar is frozen meanwhile. The eraser never threw on edge inputs (0×0, 1×1, NaN, noise), and stacked glyphs stayed intact.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: Run the eraser in a worker or OffscreenCanvas, or cap the seeds tried per column band.

qolFindings.title: Re-importing a sheet that was already saved creates silent duplicates
qolFindings.scenario: The operator saves a sheet, then rescans a better photo of the same page to fix errors. All the students are inserted again with no 'already present' cue; N1 only suffixes '(1)'/'(2)'.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: Mark rows whose name and date/age match an existing course student, without merging them, and require acknowledgement.

qolFindings.title: No plausibility bounds on age or date
qolFindings.scenario: AGE_PATTERN accepts three digits, so a stray rule digit can turn '17 anni' into '117 anni'. The review accepts ages 0–120, and a confident age-only row is ready. The first date on a row is always taken as the birth date, so a registration date gives age 0 and a ready row if no age is printed.
qolFindings.suggestedFix: Flag ages outside a configured course range (for example 5–99) and rows with more than one date.
